en: The national gem of the Philippines is the Philippine pearl, a rare and exceptionally large South Sea pearl primarily harvested in the waters of Palawan.
National hero Jose Rizal was only five feet and three inches tall, making him surprisingly short for such a towering and influential historical figure.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan originally involved an entire community physically lifting and carrying a complete nipa hut to help a relocating family.
The Ifugao people carved the spectacular Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains over two thousand years ago using only their bare hands and simple tools.
Filipino pediatrician Fe del Mundo made history in 1933 as the very first woman to ever be admitted to the prestigious Harvard Medical School.
The ancient pre-colonial Filipino writing system called Baybayin uses fourteen consonant-vowel symbols and three independent vowel symbols instead of a standard alphabet.
Bacolod's MassKara Festival features thousands of dancers wearing giant, smiling masks originally created to bring joy and hope during a tragic 1980s economic crisis.
The Philippine flag is the only national flag in the entire world that is legally flown with the red stripe on top during a state of war.
Emilio Aguinaldo declared Philippine independence on June 12, 1898, at the exact moment the Philippine national anthem was being played publicly for the very first time.
The smallest local government unit in the Philippines is the barangay, a term derived from the balangay, which were the ancient wooden boats used by early settlers.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his massive, dramatic masterpiece titled Spoliarium.
The Philippines holds the record for the longest Christmas season in the world, with festive celebrations officially starting in September and lasting until January.
